Daily Briefings · Sunday, October 25, 2026

Space & Defense Daily, Oct 23 to 25, 2026

A fight between Ukraine and Musk over Starlink, which is pushing Europe toward its own military satellite communications; Russia-linked drone attacks on Black Sea shipping, which are pushing NATO to harden its eastern flank; and the US Space Force moving missile-warning, GPS, and cislunar launches from ULA's delayed Vulcan rocket to SpaceX.

Recovered from the chat delivery: the wording is exact, but the original source links could not be recovered, so sources are shown as plain-text citations.

Space & Defense Daily, Oct 23 to 25, 2026

Top stories: a fight between Ukraine and Musk over Starlink, which is pushing Europe toward its own military satellite communications; Russia-linked drone attacks on Black Sea shipping, which are pushing NATO to harden its eastern flank; and the US Space Force moving missile-warning, GPS, and cislunar launches from ULA's delayed Vulcan rocket to SpaceX.

NATO

  • Bulgaria's Defence Ministry proposed letting ship commanders and fighter pilots shoot down weaponized drones without waiting for orders, after deadly strikes on merchant ships. (Oct 24) Sofia Globe: Bulgaria proposes drone shoot-down rule
  • NATO special forces tested counter-drone and electronic-warfare gear from 20 companies near Plovdiv, and Bulgarian commanders said some systems fell short of what their makers claimed. (Oct 24) AdriaDefense: NATO tests counter-drone systems in Bulgaria
  • The first NATO Reserve Committee met in Vilnius to work reserve forces into collective-defense plans. (Oct 24) Daily Baltic: NATO reserve committee meets in Vilnius
  • NATO Deputy Secretary General Radmila Shekerinska joins the E5 defense ministers in Paris today to discuss Ukraine and the Middle East. (Oct 23) NATO: Deputy Secretary General to visit France
  • Two NATO Assistant Secretaries General visited Kyiv to discuss Ukraine's winter needs and the PURL weapons-purchase program. (Oct 23) NATO: NATO officials visit Ukraine
  • NATO's Allied Command Transformation is buying portable GPS jammer kits for training. The tender should open Oct 26. NATO ACT: GNSS jammer kit tender
  • For context from Oct 20, NATO said it would send more patrol aircraft, radars, and drones to the Black Sea. Reuters via StreetInsider: NATO to send planes and drones to Black Sea

European Union

  • EU Defence Commissioner Kubilius launched a hybrid-threats strategy built on anticipation, active defense, and retaliation. (Oct 23) European Commission: How Europe can counter hybrid warfare
  • Lithuania filed the first payment request under the EU's SAFE defense-loan program, for €1.06 billion for its army and Baltic Defence Line. (Oct 22) Lithuanian Finance Ministry: First SAFE payment request
  • Cyprus asked the EU to restart talks on its mutual-defense clause, but it isn't on any upcoming summit agenda. (Oct 22) Politico Europe: Cyprus pushes EU mutual defense
  • For context from Oct 14, Kubilius urged member states not to cut defense and space spending in the EU's 2028 to 2034 budget. Politico Europe: Kubilius on the EU defense budget
  • There was no fresh news on the EU Space Act, which is still waiting for a position from a Parliament committee. The European Post: EU Space Act under pressure

United States

  • Because Vulcan is delayed, the Space Force moved a missile-warning satellite and cislunar payloads to Falcon Heavy, and moved three GPS launches and a Space Development Agency mission to SpaceX. (Oct 24) SpaceNews: Space Force shifts missions to SpaceX
  • Space Force leaders want extra jamming equipment so units can absorb losses in a war. (Oct 23) SpaceNews: Space Force builds jamming depth
  • Space Systems Command gave six commercial space-tracking firms, including LeoLabs and Slingshot, its first operational contracts under the civil reserve program, worth $1.37M in total. (Oct 23) Breaking Defense: First CASR contracts
  • The Pentagon and Lockheed agreed on a 10-year framework for at least 850 F-35s. Congress still has to authorize and fund it. (Oct 22) Military Times: 10-year F-35 deal
  • NASA is keeping its launch-vehicle and lander options open to save a crewed Moon landing in 2028. (Oct 23) SpaceNews: NASA and the 2028 Artemis landing
  • HawkEye 360 launched six more signals-intelligence satellites, for 39 in total. (Oct 23) SpaceNews: HawkEye 360 launches six satellites
  • There was no fresh Golden Dome or NDAA news. The defense bill has been pushed to after the Nov 3 election. (Oct 20) Defense News: Army role in Golden Dome

European space

  • ESA says the engine issues that delayed Ariane 6 are resolved. (Oct 23) SpaceNews: Ariane 6 engine issues resolved
  • The planned Airbus, Leonardo, and Thales satellite merger is stalling over EU antitrust doubts, and OHB is threatening legal action. (Oct 23) Politico Europe: Satellite merger tests space independence
  • The ESA Council prepared for the Dec 15 ministerial meeting in Rome and named two new directors. (Oct 22) ESA: 350th Council outcomes
  • Nokia and ICEYE signed a letter of intent with Ukraine's Defence Ministry to explore sovereign satellite communications. (Oct 22) Nokia: Partnership with Ukraine MoD
  • Italian media report that a Leonardo and Rheinmetall joint venture won $4.16B in Italian Army vehicle contracts, though neither company has confirmed it. (Oct 23) Defense News: Leonardo and Rheinmetall contracts

Global space & defense

  • Ukraine disputed Musk's claim that its military broke Starlink's terms, and full Starlink service has been restored. (Oct 25) CNBC: Ukraine disputes Musk's Starlink claim
  • A BBC explainer finds that none of Europe's options, Eutelsat OneWeb, Govsatcom, or IRIS², can fully replace Starlink for Ukraine yet. BBC: Can Europe plug the Starlink gap?
  • Ukrainian strikes cut power in occupied Crimea, and the UK and France are running a joint exercise in Germany. (Oct 25) The Guardian: Ukraine war briefing
  • China launched its 28th batch of Guowang internet satellites, putting about 231 in orbit. (Oct 24) Spaceflight News: China's 28th Guowang launch
